heroManifesto: Not just a score. A faster path into the next draft.
heroBody: This beta version of the IELTS Writing Checker already supports Task 1 review, Task 2 review, and history viewing.
storyBody: This beta is focused on the core writing review loop: submit, inspect feedback, and return to previous reports.
featureListItemOne: Task 1 review with image upload for charts, tables, and diagrams.
featureListItemTwo: Task 2 review with band scoring, inline revisions, and priority fixes.
featureListItemThree: History viewing for previous review results and linked originals.
sectionTwoTitle: Task 1 already supports image upload before review.
sectionTwoBody: For charts, tables, diagrams, and similar prompts, users can upload the source image first and then submit the Task 1 response for review.
sectionTwoPointOneBody: The browser compresses the image before object storage upload, so the review flow stays lighter.
sectionTwoPointTwoBody: History records can reopen the original image that was attached to that specific review.
sectionTwoPointThreeBody: This fits real Task 1 study better because users do not need to manually rewrite the whole prompt.
sectionThreeTitle: Task 2 review is built for rewrite cycles, not just one-off scoring.
sectionThreeBody: Beyond the overall band, it gives inline edits, priority fixes, and a clearer path into the next draft.
sectionThreeNoteBody: Read the score first, then switch into revise mode and inspect each change before writing the next version.
sectionFourTitle: Each review can come back later inside your own history timeline.
sectionFourBody: Signed-in users can revisit old reports and reconnect the score, original text, original image, and review context in one place.
sectionFourListOne: Reopen previous Task 1 and Task 2 results
sectionFourListTwo: See the linked original essay and uploaded image
sectionFourListThree: Use old reports as reference for the next rewrite
sectionFiveTitle: This is still a beta, so feedback matters.
sectionFiveBody: If a score feels off, a step feels awkward, or a feature is missing, keep sending product feedback from the navbar entry.
sectionFiveHintBody: Specific notes are best: tell us which task type you used, where the workflow broke, and what result you expected instead.
featureOneBody: Rubric-based scoring with a clear breakdown for task achievement, cohesion, vocabulary and grammar.
featureTwoBody: Each correction stays attached to the essay so users can inspect what changed and why.
featureThreeBody: Task switching, target band and usage tracking stay in one place instead of being split across screens.
colorsTitleRest: review modes for different writing goals
colorsBody: Use the same checker for task practice, quick scoring, revision study and account-linked sessions.
ctaTitle: A checker that fits your workflow.
ctaBody: Open the writing checker, choose Task 1 or Task 2, then run a full review with inline feedback and band scoring.
detailsHighlightBodyOne: The landing page now follows the Around product layout much more closely: large visual hero, centered media section, split CTA rows, detail columns and a gallery finish.
detailsHighlightBodyTwo: The copy and images are placeholders for now. The important part is that the page structure, rhythm and component hierarchy match the original template style.
galleryTitle: Take another look at the checker.
galleryBody: These gallery blocks mirror the original product landing composition and can be replaced later with real IELTS-specific visuals.
galleryCardOneBody: Use large visual blocks to present the scoring, revision and study experience.
galleryCardTwoBody: Turn the landing page into a product story first, then route users into the working checker.
